name: Cause and Effect
shortcutSummary: Identify which event could have led to the other. The cause always precedes the effect in time. If both events are independent or consequences of a common cause, neither is the cause of the other.
conceptExplanation: Cause and Effect questions present two statements and ask you to identify the causal relationship: Is Statement I the cause and II the effect? Vice versa? Are both effects of a common cause? Or are they independent?

subtopics.name: Cause and Effect — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Cause and Effect questions present two statements and ask you to identify the causal relationship: Is Statement I the cause and II the effect? Vice versa? Are both effects of a common cause? Or are they independent?
shortcuts: Time Sequence: The cause must come before the effect chronologically.
Direct Link Test: Can you logically explain how one event leads to the other?
Common Cause Possibility: Both events might be effects of an unstated third event.
